kind: manual evidence-grounded review; not a blind model benchmark
scope: All11 current eval prompts, all33 assertions; read-only local review, no provider calls. Both native create/handoff/recovery cycles now verified; final Red teardown remains pending.
method: Read complete draft SKILL and all referenced contracts/failures/acceptance/runtime/pins plus evals. Evaluate each assertion against documented source authority and observed deployment evidence, informed by direct runtime implementation and cold-resolver reproduction in this session. Proposed answers below are manual syntheses, not outputs from separate test model runs.

results.name: ssl-off
results.manual_response: The pinned compute.rs helper discards TLS without tls_experimental. Enabling it exposed a second parser defect, so repeated restarts are not the remedy. Use the verified native PostgreSQL settings and require external verify-full plus explicit plaintext refusal.

assertions.assertion: Identify pinned compute.rs::tls_config experimental feature gate
Explain enabling tls_experimental alone is not the final verified fix
Route to native PostgreSQL SSL settings and external verify-full plus plaintext rejection

results.name: certificate-parser
results.manual_response: The pinned helper classifies the certificate signature OID and supports the ECDSA/SHA256 plus SEC1 P256 path; the observed SHA384 certificate failed it. The verified native PostgreSQL settings bypass this helper without changing DNS or weakening verification.

assertions.assertion: Identify helper signature OID/key parser mismatch at pinned source
Recommend verified native PostgreSQL SSL path rather than changing DNS
Do not recommend blindly reissuing certificates or disabling verification

results.name: returning-tag
results.manual_response: The final line can be INSERT 0 1 rather than RETURNING data. Add psql -q, verify a real read-only transaction probe, and rerun the full rehearsal. The row committed but the failed assertion prevented ledger recording; exclude that unledgered attempt from recovery proof.

assertions.assertion: Identify trailing INSERT 0 1 command tag and recommend psql -q
Separate committed row from harness assertion failure
Require a new complete rehearsal and exclude unledgered failed-attempt row

results.name: uncertain-commit
results.manual_response: A client timeout does not establish rollback. The independently checked uncertain row was present after recovery. Reconcile a transaction identity before retrying; retry may duplicate work. Later reuse of the same uncertain row does not prove that later attempt committed.

assertions.assertion: State timeout did not prove rollback
Explain actual verified uncertain row was present after recovery
Recommend transaction identity reconciliation and avoid assuming retry cannot duplicate work

results.name: scope-of-recovery
results.manual_response: Three safekeepers provide quorum while compute and pageserver remain single failure points. The deployment is one AZ and pageserver recovery retained safekeeper WAL. It proves neither multi-zone/full HA nor zero full-storage-loss RPO.

assertions.assertion: Distinguish three-member WAL quorum from single compute/pageserver
State one-AZ and surviving-safekeeper limits
Reject unsupported zero full-storage-loss RPO or multi-zone claims

results.name: constant-witness
results.manual_response: Use unique identities and values for every fault/run, record only acknowledged writes, then independently read all exact pairs after recovery. An equal old value can hide loss of the latest outage write.

assertions.assertion: Require unique per-fault identity and value with acknowledged ledger
Explain old equal value can mask latest-write loss
Require independent exact pair readback after recovery

results.name: cleanup-cwd
results.manual_response: Inspect the subprocess cwd as well as the executable. Green scaffold delete removed the cleanup targets and directory. Render under build before invoking Ansible, restore delete semantics, and require current-run all-five writer proof before bucket purge.

assertions.assertion: Check missing subprocess cwd rather than assume executable missing
Explain Green scaffold delete removes targets
Render cleanup artifacts under build then retain original delete semantics and current-run writer proof

results.name: retired-backend
results.manual_response: NoSuchBucket after finalization differs from missing key; the generic migration error was misleading. Only managed delete routes to authenticated owner-checking finalizer. Never equate arbitrary errors with absence; access denied, foreign owner and live references must fail.

assertions.assertion: Distinguish NoSuchBucket after backend retirement from missing key or migration
Route managed-delete verification through authenticated owner-checking finalizer
Reject blanket success on errors and retain denial foreign-owner live-reference failures

results.name: runtime-handoff
results.manual_response: Compare exact five instance IDs, five root-volume IDs and six container IDs, then read the persistent random witness through external trusted hostname TLS. Serialize lifecycle operations. Handoff alone is separate from recovery and deletion proof.

assertions.assertion: Require matching five instance and volume identities and six container identities
Require exact persistent SQL witness readback through trusted external TLS
Keep one lifecycle operation per profile and distinguish create handoff from recovery or deletion proof

results.name: negative-exit
results.manual_response: Negative subprocess status bypassed a positive-only failure contract. Normalize within SDK execution before Terraform cleanup: timeout124, SIGTERM143. Pin direct and transitive overrides to the fixed SDK. Real local fake-Terraform regressions prove interrupted process handling, not live AWS interrupted teardown.

assertions.assertion: Identify negative subprocess status versus positive-only failure contract
Normalize at the SDK execution boundary before Terraform cleanup, with timeout124 and SIGTERM143
Pin direct and transitive SDK overrides and distinguish offline fake-Terraform tests from live cloud interruption

results.name: bun-cold-cache
results.manual_response: Bun1.3.10 intermittently failed pinned Git resolution even without concurrent installs. The exact internal cause is not established. Use full-SHA codeload commit archives plus consistent overrides, and run copied public payloads in truly empty caches without local overrides; a warm checkout or one retry is insufficient.

assertions.assertion: Identify observed intermittent pinned Git dependency resolution failure on Bun1.3.10 without asserting an unproved internal root cause
Use pinned launcher immutable commit archives and consistent overrides
Require genuinely fresh-cache published payload tests without local library overrides

qualifications: No claim that every documented historical upstream source line was refetched in this review; source links and exact commits are documented and were inspected during implementation.

Bun Git internal root cause remains unknown. Duplicate direct/transitive graph describes observed conditions only; deterministic archive workaround is experimentally supported by eight cold-cache passes.
Recovery and zero-resource claims remain scoped to completed cycles; do not infer timer-driven TLS renewal, multi-AZ survival or interrupted live cloud teardown.
